import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I’ll read the two registered reports and the three earlier studies, then investigate the gaps and disagreements before writing a consolidated recommendation. I’m using the SASE repository, artifact, and memory workflows to preserve provenance.


The reports disagree on two important points: whether “follow” is useful beyond controlling data loading, and what makes agent reads slow. I’ll check the read paths and lifecycle code, and keep the UX distinction between browsing the fleet and choosing which work to manage close at hand.


The code supports researcher B’s performance concern: CLI listing still scans artifacts, while ACE has an index-backed path. I also confirmed that the shared loader checks local PIDs and repairs local files, so remote records cannot safely enter it unchanged. I’m leaning toward two views over one list widget: **Focus** for local and followed work, and **Fleet** for remote browsing.


My profile confirms that scanning and conversion dominate: `sase agent list --json` took 11.7 seconds, including two Rust scans totaling 6.5 seconds. Removing interpreter startup alone will not fix that. The recommendation will also retain the requested `%dispatch` spelling and treat gate approvals as potentially command-executing mutations, with the same retry protections as other remote actions.


The consolidated draft is written, and both source reports have been moved and verified byte for byte. It resolves several gaps beyond the two reports: preventing recursive re-export of followed agents, preserving identity across transport changes, following families through gates and monitors, and distinguishing an unsent launch from one whose acceptance is uncertain. I’m checking the final layout, links, and report now.


The layout, relative links, Markdown checks, and original-file hashes all pass. The report is registered as a durable artifact; neither code checkout changed. I’m using the SASE finalizer skill now to declare the research report and preserved source moves complete.


Created the [consolidated report](/home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_12/sase/repos/research/202609/remote_dispatch_and_fleet_focus/remote_dispatch_and_fleet_focus.md), with both original reports preserved unchanged alongside it.

The recommendation is:

- Keep `%dispatch:<machine>` and automatic following.
- Use **Focus / Fleet** views over one Agents list.
- Provide lazy access plugins, with Tailnet enabled by default and HTTPS as an alternative.
- Fix indexed reads, portable identity, and mutation recovery before exposing remote controls.

The report resolves the researchers’ disagreements, adds fresh profiling evidence, and includes UX mockups, failure behavior, and delivery stages. File integrity and links passed verification.
